<August 21>
Through the winding gorge I came at last to
the Black Pass, with the tower of Eisen far off.
For a while I stared, as though dazed, at the
shadow of the mist-shrouded tower.
Below me lay pastures, a scattering of houses,
and a small church at the center of the village.
The faint gloom I sense about this village—
is it only the fault of the dismal weather?
Already I am reduced to pining for the bustle
of the great city of London.
